svg.title: What happens when an agent opens this repo cold
svg.desc: A trace of one real session on 2026-08-26. Seven questions an agent needed answered while working in the repo, and where each answer actually came from. One: what are the rules here – answered by the docs, because CLAUDE.md loads automatically. Two: what documents exist – no index linked them, so it was found by running a filesystem search. Three: what is the system and what are its contracts – answered by the docs, via core.design.md. Four: what states does one component have – partial, because twenty component contracts live in one table and the answer sits in a two-hundred-word cell. Five: are the brand values still current – unanswerable, because the values are hand-copied from build output and nothing verifies them. Six: what does an npm consumer actually receive – no document says, so it was answered by running npm pack. Seven: what work is underway right now – the backlog on main does not mention it, so it was answered by the human, and the document turned out to be on an unpushed branch. Two of seven questions were answered by the documentation, one partially, and four required searching, running commands, or asking a person.
svg.text: A reader's journey
What happened when an agent opened this repo cold. A trace of one real session, 2026-08-26 – not a hypothetical.
WHAT IT NEEDED TO KNOW
WHERE THE ANSWER ACTUALLY CAME FROM
“What are the rules here?”
Before touching a single file.
ANSWERED BY THE DOCS
CLAUDE.md loads automatically. Invariants, semantic-tokens-only,
the density trap, “flagging is not permission”. All of it landed.
“What documents exist?”
The question that started this session.
FOUND BY SEARCHING THE FILESYSTEM
No index links them. Ran find . -name "*.md" and read the
result. A reader who cannot run commands gets nothing here.
“What is the system?”
Token shape, contracts, how to add a brand.
ANSWERED BY THE DOCS
core.design.md. The YAML said what exists; the prose said what it
means. Both registers were needed – neither alone would do.
“What states does Chip have?”
One component, in detail.
PARTIAL
A 200-word cell inside a 20-row table. Readable, but nothing to
link to, nothing to diff, and no way to check it against the code.
“Are these values still true?”
The brand files' YAML frontmatter.
UNANSWERABLE
Hand-copied from the build output, with nothing checking them.
The most structured layer in the repo has the weakest guarantee.
“What does a user receive?”
Thomas asked whether the backlog ships.
ANSWERED BY RUNNING CODE
No document states it. Ran npm pack --dry-run. The system
cannot say where it ends, so nobody can say what to rely on.
“What work is underway?”
The single most important current fact.
ANSWERED BY THE HUMAN
The backlog on main never mentions the token review. Thomas had
to ask. Found via git branch – it sits on an unpushed branch.
Two of seven questions were answered by the documentation. One partially. Four were not.
Those four were recovered by searching the filesystem, running a build command, and asking Thomas directly – none of which
an external consumer can do. The failures cluster into three fixes: an index that links, a check that proves freshness, and reach.
Green = the docs answered it. Amber = the docs made it hard. Red = the docs could not answer it at all.
